description: Independent email comprehension EN/B1 draft; human review required.

tabs.title: A Changing Neighbourhood
tabs.description: Understand what has happened in the square.

questions.q: Why does Tomas remember the old square with a different feeling now?
choices: It has been closed to everyone.
It no longer has any shops.
It is now outside the town.
It has become a more active community place.
questions.explanation: The square's workshop and painted walls show a positive change from the old empty shop.

questions.q: What do the photographs in the workshop help visitors discover?
choices: How to make the newest bicycles.
How the neighbourhood has changed over time.
Which films are shown this week.
Why nobody uses the square today.
questions.explanation: The old photos and Mrs Okafor's stories preserve the square's history.

questions.q: Why could Robin's photographs be useful at the open day?
choices: They would be used as entrance tickets.
They would replace all the volunteers.
They could show everyday local life and add to the shared stories.
They would prove that the cinema is still open.
questions.explanation: Tomas remembers Robin's pictures as suitable material for the community event.

questions.q: What did Tomas learn after teaching children to fix a bicycle light?
choices: Being helpful does not require being an expert.
He should become a professional mechanic immediately.
The workshop is only for adults.
Making tea is the only useful job there.
questions.explanation: He reflects that people can contribute while they are still learning.

questions.q: Why did Tomas begin with simple jobs at the workshop?
choices: He wanted to avoid all practical work.
The workshop had no tools available.
He had already finished repairing everything.
He felt uncertain about meeting unfamiliar people.
questions.explanation: Tomas says nervousness made him start by making tea and carrying boxes.

questions.q: What does Mrs Okafor contribute that the pictures alone cannot provide?
choices: A full set of new football boots.
Personal memories and stories about the places shown.
Instructions for painting the walls.
Tickets for the old cinema.
questions.explanation: She knows stories behind the old photographs.

questions.q: Why does Tomas mention travel costs when inviting Robin?
choices: He recognises that visiting may not be easy for his friend.
He is asking Robin to pay for the workshop.
He wants to stop the open day.
He is making an excuse not to meet.
questions.explanation: Tomas respects Robin's possible practical difficulties without making him feel guilty.

questions.q: What does the suggestion of a video call reveal about Tomas's goal?
choices: He thinks video calls are better than any friendship.
He wants Robin to give a speech online.
He wants to reconnect even if Robin cannot attend in person.
He plans to close the workshop soon.
questions.explanation: Tomas offers more than one way to restore their conversation.

questions.q: How does Tomas try to make the invitation less stressful?
choices: He requires Robin to bring a full exhibition.
He says a short visit is enough and no special preparation is needed.
He expects Robin to lead all activities.
He refuses to discuss other dates.
questions.explanation: The invitation explicitly avoids pressure to perform.

questions.q: What important change does Tomas want in their friendship?
choices: To stop sharing any photographs.
To work in the same town every day.
To use only public social media comments.
To communicate regularly rather than wait for special occasions.
questions.explanation: The closing question asks them not to wait for a special event before speaking.
